cards.explanation: The answer is to meet him face to face. Amaziah, king of Judah, sends word to Jehoash, king of Israel, and says, “Come, let us meet face to face…” (2 Chronicles 25:17). Sounds friendly, doesn't it? I think a message like that could mean a lot of things, and the next verses show it wasn't a friendly chat, friends.

The answer is a wild beast tramples it. Jehoash, king of Israel, says, “Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.” (2 Chronicles 25:18). Short story, and the ending is rough on the thistle, friends. That thistle went in asking for a wedding and came out flat.

The answer is True. Jehoash, king of Israel, says to Amaziah, “You have said, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom,’ and your heart has become proud and boastful.” (2 Chronicles 25:19). He doesn't dance around it, bakers. He repeats Amaziah's own words about Edom and then says his heart has become proud and boastful.

The answer is home. Jehoash tells Amaziah, king of Judah, “Now stay at home.” (2 Chronicles 25:19). Four words and a whole lot of sense, friends. I stayed put in a junk drawer for years, so trust me, it can be done.

The answer is False. Jehoash says, “Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?” (2 Chronicles 25:19). Amaziah isn't the only one in that warning, bakers, because Judah is named right alongside him. That's the part that stings.

The answer is that they had sought the gods of Edom. The writer says this had come from God “…because they had sought the gods of Edom.” (2 Chronicles 25:20). Edom, the nation Amaziah says he defeated, had gods of its own, and Judah went looking to them. The text gives the reason plainly, friends, so I won't add one.

The answer is that they all scatter and run away. The text says Judah “…was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his own home.” (2 Chronicles 25:22). Every man heads for his own front door, friends. I think that's what happens when the plan falls apart and nobody wants to be the last one standing.

The answer is False. Jehoash captured Amaziah at Beth-shemesh, and the text says it happened “There at Beth-shemesh…” (2 Chronicles 25:23). The army scatters, but Amaziah is captured, bakers. He asked for a face to face meeting, and he got one.

The answer is that he breaks down a long section of it. Jehoash “…broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.” (2 Chronicles 25:23). That's a big stretch of wall, friends, and it's Jerusalem's own wall. A city feels that one.

The answer is hostages. The text says Jehoash took the gold, the silver and the articles, “…as well as some hostages.” (2 Chronicles 25:24). Then he returned to Samaria. He took treasure from the house of God and the royal palace treasuries, bakers, and people went with him too.

The answer is Lachish. The text says Amaziah “…fled to Lachish.” (2 Chronicles 25:27). He runs there with a conspiracy behind him, friends. The men sent after him still find him there. The story of Amaziah's reign ends here.
